content: {"summary":"A Sentinel failover on 12 Nov 2025 caused auth‑service‑02 to keep writing to the old Redis primary, which returned READONLY errors. Those writes failed, the session was never stored, and subsequent lookups produced AUTH‑E401X, creating the observed spike despite redis‑sessions‑02 being up.","likely_cause":"Sentinel‑initiated Redis failover left auth‑service‑02 writing to a demoted primary, causing READONLY write failures and lost session writes, which manifested as an AUTH‑E401X spike.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The AUTH‑E401X spike aligns with a Redis primary change (failover).","evidence_ids":["RB-018#0"],"quote":"A spike that lines up with a redis-sessions primary change points at Redis."},{"text":"During failover, writes to the demoted primary return READONLY errors.","evidence_ids":["RB-018#1"],"quote":"write sent to it gets `READONLY You can't write against a read only replica.`"},{"text":"A READONLY write failure means the session is never stored, leading to AUTH‑E401X on the next request.","evidence_ids":["RB-018#2"],"quote":"the session is never stored."},{"text":"A similar October 2025 failover caused users of the instance that hadn’t learned the new primary to see AUTH‑E401X.","evidence_ids":["RB-018#4"],"quote":"were asked to log in again on their next request (`AUTH-E401X`)."}],"next_checks":["Check Sentinel logs for the exact failover timestamp on 12 Nov 2025","Verify which Redis node was primary before and after the failover","Inspect auth‑service‑02 logs for READONLY errors around the failover time","Confirm that redis‑sessions‑02 remained up and was the new primary"]}
